newsitem.title: UK: B.Gas now solved 20 pct of contract problems.
newsitem.headline: B.Gas now solved 20 pct of contract problems.

text.p: The renegotiation with Mobil Corp means that British Gas Plc has now solved around 20 percent of its long term "take or pay" gas contracts problems, a company spokesman told Reuters.
The spokesman said that British Gas has a total of 30.5 billion stg of contracts, but it does not want to renegotiate all of them.

A first round of renegotiations with British Petroleum Co Plc and British Gas' own exploration and production arm was announced on December 5, and chairman Richard Giordano said at the time that these contracts, worth 293 million stg, accounted for around 10 percent of all contracts it wanted to renegotiate.

But the spokesman would not put a more exact figure on the value of Monday's deal. Nor would he comment on the timing of any future deals, except to say that negotiations are continuing with other companies.

Under the new agreement, Centrica, the new British Gas unit to be formed by the company's demerger set for February, will reduce its long term commitment to buy gas from Mobil by cancelling two contracts.
And on three other contracts, prices will be reduced to market levels on a phased basis. This will reduce the price and volume commitment on 10 billion therms, British Gas said in a statement.

In return, British Gas will transfer to Mobil North Sea Ltd some producing and transportation assets in and around the Beryl field. These include five percent of the Beryl field itself, 29.5 percent of Block 9/12a in the Nevis field, and 2.5 percent of the SAGE pipeline system.
This will give Mobil an extra 27 million barrels of oil equivalent (boe) of reserves, and an extra 9,000 boe per day of production.
